sbtk.interior.align_with_spin_axis#

Set the axis of components along the axis of the largest moment of the whole model.

Syntax

MATLAB
[interior, axis_dir, iterations] = sbtk.interior.align_with_spin_axis(body, interior, names, tol_deg, max_iter)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredthe body Fields: body.
interior1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.interior.create Fields: interior.
names1 × anystringrequiredthe components to align (string array; tori, ellipsoids or sectors), e.g. "torus"; strings(1, 0) for none
tol_degscalardoubledegrequiredconvergence: the axis moves by at most this angle in the last iteration [deg] Validation: mustBePositive.
max_iterscalardoublerequiredlargest number of iterations (sbtk:iteration:notConverged beyond it) Validation: mustBeInteger, mustBePositive.

Outputs

NameDescription
interiorfrom sbtk.interior.create Fields: interior.
axis_dir1 x 3 axis of the largest moment of the aligned interior, in the frame of the shape model (pointing to +z's side)
iterationsnumber of simulations made

Description

A body in principal-axis rotation spins about its axis of the largest moment, so a component that formed about the spin axis, such as an equatorial torus, lies about that axis. The axis depends on every component, the aligned ones included, so the alignment is a fixed-point iteration (sbtk.internal.fixed_point): simulate to degree 2, take the axis of the largest moment (sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame), turn the named components to it (sbtk.interior.set_axis), repeat. Each iteration is one simulation; the axis usually settles to 0.01 deg in 2 to 4.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, core.
t = sbtk.interior.torus("torus", 0.370, 0.055, 0, -500);
t.center_km = body.centroid_km;
interior = sbtk.interior.create([core, t], sbtk.interior.no_random_field());
[interior, axis_dir] = sbtk.interior.align_with_spin_axis(body, interior, "torus", 0.01, 20);
fprintf('axis %.2f deg from the shape-model z-axis\n', acosd(axis_dir(3)));

Related functions

Calls

  t = sbtk.interior.set_axis(t, [sind(5) 0 cosd(5)]);         % axis tilted 5 deg toward +x

sbtk.interior.to_frame#

An interior or a true model in another frame: x' = (x - origin_km) * axes.

Syntax

MATLAB
model = sbtk.interior.to_frame(model, origin_km, axes)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
model1 × 1structrequiredan interior (sbtk.interior.create) or a true model (truth from sbtk.data.simulate)
origin_km1 × 3doublekmrequiredorigin of the new frame in the current frame [km]; [0 0 0] keeps the origin Validation: mustBeFinite.
axes3 × 3doublerequired3 x 3 rotation, columns: the new axes as unit vectors in the current frame, e.g. cf.axes of sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame; eye(3) keeps the axes Validation: mustBeFinite.

Outputs

NameDescription
modelan interior (sbtk.interior.create) or a true model (truth from sbtk.data.simulate)

Description

Every position is transformed as x' = (x - origin_km)*axes and every direction as d' = d*axes: the centers of spheres, ellipsoids and tori, the axes of ellipsoids, tori and sectors (c.axes), the random field, and for a true model origin_km and com_km. Its coefficients are rotated (exact, sbtk.internal.sh_rotation) and its inertia elements become axes'*I*axes; both stay about the same point. The density at every point of the body is unchanged, so the model, the body from sbtk.body.to_frame and the measurements from sbtk.data.to_frame (same origin_km and axes) describe the same body in the new frame: simulating, gridding, plotting and comparing there gives the transformed results. An inversion result cannot be transformed: transform the measurements and the body and invert in the new frame.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, interior.
[exact, truth] = sbtk.data.simulate(body, interior, 4, "T1");
spin  = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(truth, body, "spin");   % origin: center of mass; z: largest moment
truth_s = sbtk.interior.to_frame(truth, spin.com_km, spin.axes);
body_s  = sbtk.body.to_frame(body, spin.com_km, spin.axes, "didymos_com_spin_axes");
grid = sbtk.exchange.density_grid(body_s, truth_s, 0.020);         % the grid in the new frame

sbtk.interior.torus#

Uniform torus component about the z-axis, clipped to the body.

Syntax

MATLAB
c = sbtk.interior.torus(name, ring_radius_km, tube_radius_km, height_km, drho_kgm3)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription

ring_radius_kmscalardoublekmrequiredradius of the tube's center circle [km] Validation: mustBeNonnegative.

Outputs

NameDescription

Description

The torus lies about the z-axis of the shape-model frame (c.center_km = [0 0 0], c.axes = eye(3); sbtk.interior.to_frame moves and turns both with the frame). It may be buried, intersect the surface or extend outside the body; only its intersection with the body counts. sbtk.interior.set_axis turns it; sbtk.interior.align_with_spin_axis puts it about the model's own axis of the largest moment. An inversion can estimate its center (c.estimate_position = true, or a mask such as [false false true] for z only) and the direction of its axis (c.estimate_axis = true) besides its density (sbtk.invert.run).

sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame#

A gravity field about its center of mass, in the shape-model, spin or principal axes.

Syntax

MATLAB
cf = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(set, body, axes)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
set1 × 1structrequiredthe field: a measurement set (sbtk.data.simulate, sbtk.exchange.read_data, sbtk.exchange.read_shadr, ...), a true model (truth from sbtk.data.simulate) or an inversion result (fit from sbtk.invert.run: the field of the fitted model)
body1 × 1structrequiredthe body: the shape model for a fitted model, the reference radius for a true model or a fitted model Fields: body.
axes1 × 1stringrequired"shape": the axes of the shape-model frame; "spin": z along the axis of the largest moment of the field (the spin axis of a body in principal-axis rotation), x the shape-model x-axis projected onto the plane normal to it, y = z x x: the frame of body-fixed radio-science fields such as the OSIRIS-REx field of Bennu, with C21 = S21 = 0 and S22 not 0; "principal": the principal axes of inertia of the field (x the axis of the smallest moment, z of the largest, each pointing to the positive side of the shape-model axis nearest to it, right-handed), with C21 = S21 = S22 = 0 Validation: mustBeMember(axes, ["shape", "spin", "principal"]).

Outputs

NameDescription
cfThe field about its center of mass in the chosen axes, with its principal axes and moments. Fields: cf.

Description

cf.labels1 x n names of the coefficients, 'C10' ... (degree 1 to cf.degree)
cf.coef1 x n fully normalized coefficients about the center of mass: degree 1 is 0; in spin axes C21 = S21 = 0, in principal axes C21 = S21 = S22 = 0
cf.sigma1 x n 1-sigma (NaN without uncertainties); degree 1: of the center of mass
cf.covn x n covariance (NaN without uncertainties)
cf.com_kmthe center of mass in the shape-model frame [km]
cf.axes3 x 3, columns: the axes of cf.coef as unit vectors in the shape-model axes (eye(3) for "shape"); sbtk.body.to_frame, sbtk.data.to_frame and sbtk.interior.to_frame take cf.com_km and cf.axes to express everything in the frame with the center of mass as origin and these axes
cf.principal3 x 3, columns: the principal axes (smallest, middle, largest moment) in the shape-model axes
cf.moments1 x 3 principal moments minus their mean, A <= B <= C, as I / (M R_ref^2) (the degree-2 field fixes the moments up to their trace)

cf.R_ref_km, cf.degree

Moving the expansion point to the center of mass makes degree 1 vanish: about a point O, C10, C11, S11 = (z, x, y of the center of mass - O)/(sqrt(3) R_ref). The translation of solid harmonics mixes lower degrees into higher ones (degree 2 into 3, ...), so all coefficients change; it is exact (sbtk.internal.sh_translation). Rotating the axes mixes the 2l+1 coefficients within each degree and leaves every degree's power unchanged; in the principal axes the degree-2 inertia tensor is diagonal, so C21 = S21 = S22 = 0 and C20 = (A + B - 2C)/(2 M R^2), C22 = (B - A)/(4 M R^2) (unnormalized). The rotation is exact too (sbtk.internal.sh_rotation). In the spin axes only the tilt of the axis of the largest moment is removed: C21 = S21 = 0, and the angle of the axis of the smallest moment from x is (1/2) atan2(S22, C22).

The center of mass: a true model's com_km; a fitted model's own center of mass (computed from its densities); for a measurement set, origin_km plus the offset its degree-1 coefficients give. A measurement set with coef_about 'origin' whose degree-1 coefficients put the center of mass more than 3 sigma from origin_km (more than 1 mm for exact values), e.g. a SHADR field about the shape-model origin, is moved to that center of mass; otherwise it is taken as about its center of mass already (its degree-1 values are then noise about zero). A set without degree-1 coefficients (e.g. sbtk.io.read_jpl_gravity) is taken as about its center of mass, origin_km; its degree-1 sigma is NaN. Moving a set and the principal axes need every coefficient of degree >= 2 up to the set's degree; a set that lacks some can be used only with axes "shape" and only if it is about its center of mass (missing coefficients are NaN).

The covariance is propagated through the translation and the rotation as linear maps; the uncertainty of the center of mass and of the principal axes themselves, which the data also determine, is not added.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, interior.
[exact, truth] = sbtk.data.simulate(body, interior, 4, "T1");
cs = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(truth, body, "shape");       % degree 1 = 0
cz = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(truth, body, "spin");        % and C21 = S21 = 0
cp = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(truth, body, "principal");   % and C21 = S21 = S22 = 0
disp([cs.labels(1:8); string(cs.coef(1:8)); string(cp.coef(1:8))])
tilt_deg = acosd(cp.principal(3, 3))         % largest-moment axis from the shape z-axis

sbtk.gravity.component_integrals#

Integrals over one component per unit density, clipped to the body.

Syntax

MATLAB
I = sbtk.gravity.component_integrals(geo, c)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
geo1 × 1structrequiredGeometry from sbtk.gravity.geometry: the expansion origin and degree of the integrals. Fields: geo.
c1 × 1structrequiredOne component. Fields: component.

Outputs

NameDescription
IIntegrals of the part of the component inside the body, per unit density. Fields: integrals.

Description

I.U1 x (L+1)^2 int (r/R)^l Ybar_lm dV (packed as geo.pk) [km^3]
I.Vvolume [km^3]
I.m1first moment [km^4]
I.Qsecond moments [xx yy zz xy xz yz] [km^5]

all about geo.origin_km and limited to the body.

A sphere entirely inside the body is an exact point mass. Every other component is integrated ray by ray: each interval of a sub-ray inside the component, between scaled facets s_a and s_b, adds its exact cone-scaling integrals (see sbtk.gravity.geometry). Layers and sectors give the interval directly; for spheres, ellipsoids and tori the crossings of each ray with their surface are the real roots of a quadratic (sphere, ellipsoid) or quartic (torus) in the distance along the ray, so a ray may cross a component any number of times and the integrals change smoothly with the component's geometry.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body.
geo = sbtk.gravity.geometry(body, [0 0 0], 4);
I = sbtk.gravity.component_integrals(geo, sbtk.interior.sphere("core", [0 0 0], 0.170, 0));
fprintf('volume inside the body %.4f km^3\n', I.V);

sbtk.gravity.geometry#

Facet-cone geometry of a body about an expansion origin (the integration workspace).

Syntax

MATLAB
geo = sbtk.gravity.geometry(body, origin_km, degree)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.body.create Fields: body.
origin_km1 × 3doublekmrequiredexpansion origin in shape-model coordinates [km] (1x3). Gravity coefficients, first moments and inertia are all about this point; layers and sectors are measured along rays from it. Validation: mustBeFinite.
degreescalardoublerequiredhighest spherical-harmonic degree (0 when only volumes, inertia or densities are needed: much faster) Validation: mustBeInteger, mustBeNonnegative.

Outputs

NameDescription
geoThe facet-cone geometry and integrals. Fields: geo.

Description

The body is the union of tetrahedral cones with apex at the origin and a surface facet as base. For every cone geo stores, per unit density,

Tspherical-harmonic integrals int (r/R)^l Ybar_lm dV [km^3] (nf x (L+1)^2)
Vvolume [km^3], m1 first moment [km^4],
Qsecond moments [xx yy zz xy xz yz] [km^5]

(T from the polyhedral kernel sbtk.internal.ComputePolyhedralCSBar_mex). Shrinking a cone about its apex by s multiplies r^l dV by s^(l+3), so the portion of a cone between the scaled facets s_a and s_b contributes exactly T (s_b^(l+3) - s_a^(l+3)), V (s_b^3 - s_a^3), m1 (s_b^4 - s_a^4), Q (s_b^5 - s_a^5). Interior components are described by such radial intervals along 9 sub-rays of every cone (sbtk.gravity.component_integrals).

geo fields (km units throughout)

  body, origin_km, degree, R_ref_km, pk (coefficient packing, sbtk.internal.sh_packing)
  nf, K                 number of facets, sub-rays per facet (9)
  faces, verts          mesh with vertices relative to origin_km
  D, E, F, det6, EF, FD, DE    facet corners, 6 x cone volumes, edge cross products
  T, V, m1, Q           per-cone integrals (above)
  U_body, V_body, m1_body, Q_body   whole-body sums
  ray_t, ray_dir        sub-ray surface distances [km] and unit directions (nf*K rows)

Didymos (49,152 facets): about 1 s at degree 4.

Errors when some facet faces the origin (shape not star-shaped about it).

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body.
geo = sbtk.gravity.geometry(body, body.centroid_km, 4);
fprintf('%d facets, volume %.4f km^3\n', geo.nf, geo.V_body);

sbtk.data.add_center_of_mass#

Add degree-1 coefficients that place the center of mass at a given point.

sbtk.data.add_libration#

Add a measured libration ratio (B - A)/C.

Syntax

MATLAB
obs = sbtk.data.add_libration(obs, ratio, ratio_sigma, Izz_norm)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
obs1 × 1structrequiredThe measurement set; it must contain C22 and S22. Fields: obs.
ratioscalardoublerequiredmeasured (B - A)/C: A <= B are the principal moments of inertia about the axes in the xy-plane (the long and intermediate axes of a body spinning about z) and C = Izz. This is what the libration of a synchronously rotating body depends on (amplitude 2e/(3 ratio - 1) for forced libration in an orbit of eccentricity e). Validation: mustBeFinite.
ratio_sigmascalardoublerequiredits 1-sigma Validation: mustBePositive.
Izz_normscalardoubleM R_ref²requiredIzz / (M R_ref^2) used to scale the uncertainty (a homogeneous-body value is accurate enough) Validation: mustBePositive.

Outputs

NameDescription
obsThe measurement set with the libration row added. Fields: obs.

Description

The principal axes need not be the shape-model axes: their direction in the xy-plane comes from the measured C22 and S22 of obs (which must have them), and the measurement is stored as the linear row

    cos(2a) (Iyy - Ixx) + sin(2a) 2 Ixy - ratio Izz = 0 +- ratio_sigma Izz_norm,

(B - A) written with the principal-axis angle a (sbtk.internal.libration_weights). Together with C22 and S22, which give B - A, the ratio measures C to a relative precision of about ratio_sigma/ratio.

sbtk.data.libration_ratio_from_amplitude#

(B - A)/C from the forced libration of a synchronous satellite.

Syntax

MATLAB
[ratio, ratio_sigma] = sbtk.data.libration_ratio_from_amplitude(amplitude_deg, amplitude_sigma_deg, e, e_sigma)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
amplitude_degscalardoubledegrequiredsigned amplitude G of the forced libration gamma = G sin(M) [deg]: gamma is the angle of the long axis from the direction to the primary, M the mean anomaly. G < 0 (the long axis lags behind the primary direction while the satellite moves fastest) for (B - A)/C < 1/3, which covers elongations up to about 1.4 : 1; G > 0 above that. Validation: mustBeNonzero.
amplitude_sigma_degscalardoubledegrequired1-sigma of G [deg] Validation: mustBeNonnegative.
escalardoublerequiredorbital eccentricity and its 1-sigma Validation: mustBeInRange(e, 0, 1, 'exclude-upper').
e_sigmascalardoublerequiredorbital eccentricity and its 1-sigma Validation: mustBeNonnegative.

Outputs

NameDescription
ratio(B - A)/C (principal moments, see sbtk.data.add_libration) and its 1-sigma, from first-order error propagation
ratio_sigma(B - A)/C (principal moments, see sbtk.data.add_libration) and its 1-sigma, from first-order error propagation

Description

Planar forced libration in a Keplerian orbit about a point-mass primary, to first order in e: gamma'' + 3 n^2 ratio gamma = 2 e n^2 sin(M), so G = 2e/(3 ratio - 1) and ratio = (1 + 2e/G)/3. Free libration, the primary's oblateness and the mutual dynamics of a binary are not included. The sensitivity grows near ratio = 1/3, where the free libration period equals the orbital period: an elongated body gives a large amplitude and a precise ratio, a nearly axisymmetric one a small amplitude that depends little on the ratio.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: obs.
% amplitude -12 +- 0.2 deg, e = 0.027 +- 0.001: (B - A)/C = 0.247 +- 0.0035 (1.4%)
[k, sk] = sbtk.data.libration_ratio_from_amplitude(-12, 0.2, 0.027, 0.001);
obs = sbtk.data.add_libration(obs, k, sk, 0.39);
% a nearly axisymmetric body: -4.0 +- 0.2 deg gives 0.075 +- 0.016 (21%)

Related functions

Mentioned in the help text

sbtk.data.set_uncertainties#

Give measurements a 1-sigma uncertainty per degree and per inertia quantity.

Syntax

MATLAB
obs = sbtk.data.set_uncertainties(obs, unc)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
obs1 × 1structrequiredmeasurements, e.g. the exact values from sbtk.data.simulate, which have none Fields: obs.
unc1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.data.uncertainties Fields: unc.

Outputs

NameDescription
obsmeasurements, e.g. the exact values from sbtk.data.simulate, which have none Fields: obs.

Description

Every gravity coefficient of degree l gets the 1-sigma unc.coef_sigma_by_degree(l), and the coefficient covariance becomes diagonal. Every inertia element (Ixx, Iyy, Izz, Ixy, Ixz, Iyz) gets unc.moi_sigma. The libration row gets unc.libration_sigma times the Izz / (M R_ref^2) of the Izz row (set the uncertainties before sbtk.data.select_moi removes that row). Rows with other labels (sbtk.data.add_moi_row) keep their sigma. The values themselves do not change; sbtk.data.add_noise then draws noise from these uncertainties.

For other uncertainties: sbtk.data.use_uncertainties (those of another data set), sbtk.data.set_covariance (a full coefficient covariance), sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma (inertia rows by label).

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, interior.

obs = sbtk.data.add_noise(sbtk.data.set_uncertainties(exact, unc), 1);

sbtk.data.simulate#

True model of an interior and its exact gravity coefficients and moments of inertia.

Syntax

MATLAB
[exact, truth, geo] = sbtk.data.simulate(body, interior, degree, name)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.body.create (shape, total mass, reference radius) Fields: body.
interior1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.interior.create (components + random field) Fields: interior.
degreescalardoublerequiredmaximum degree of the gravity coefficients Validation: mustBeInteger, mustBePositive.
name1 × 1stringrequiredname of the data set, e.g. "didymos_T1"

Outputs

NameDescription
exactthe exact values as a measurement set (docs/data_formats.md), without uncertainties (coef_cov and every inertia sigma are NaN); for Didymos to degree 4: coef_labels 24 x 1 {'C10';'C11';'S11';'C20';...}, coef 24 x 1, moi 7 rows (Ixx Iyy Izz Ixy Ixz Iyz, I/(M R_ref^2); libration: (B - A)/C with principal moments, see sbtk.data.add_libration), origin_km the center of mass the coefficients are about [km] Fields: obs.
truththe true model (rho_bg_kgm3, components, random_field, origin_km, exact values) Fields: truth.
geogeometry about the center of mass (for plots and comparisons) Fields: geo.

Description

The gravity field and inertia are expanded about the center of mass. Layers and sectors are defined along rays from the expansion origin, so the interior, and with it the center of mass, depend on the origin: the geometry is rebuilt about the center of mass until it moves by less than 1 mm (sbtk.internal.fixed_point, at most 50 times; sbtk:iteration:notConverged otherwise). No measurement uncertainties are involved: the values are exact.

To make measurements of the true model, give the exact values uncertainties (sbtk.data.set_uncertainties: one 1-sigma per degree and per inertia quantity; sbtk.data.use_uncertainties: those of another data set; sbtk.data.set_covariance, sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma) and draw noise from them (sbtk.data.add_noise).

Errors when the density is negative anywhere.

Example

MATLAB, from the help text
body = sbtk.body.from_mass("Didymos", sbtk.shape.bundled("didymos"), 5.273e11, 0.43);
interior = sbtk.interior.create(sbtk.interior.sphere("core", [0 0 0], 0.170, +450));
[exact, truth] = sbtk.data.simulate(body, interior, 4, "T1");          % the true model
unc = sbtk.data.uncertainties([sbtk.units.offset_to_degree1(0.002, 0.43), 1e-4, 2e-4, 4e-4], 2e-3, 0.02);
obs = sbtk.data.add_noise(sbtk.data.set_uncertainties(exact, unc), 1);  % measurements of it

sbtk.data.to_frame#

A measurement set in another frame: x' = (x - origin_km) * axes.

Syntax

MATLAB
obs = sbtk.data.to_frame(obs, origin_km, axes)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
obs1 × 1structrequireda measurement set; to change the axes it must have all six inertia elements without uncertainties, as the exact values of sbtk.data.simulate have (or no inertia rows): a measurement is made in the frame it is reported in, so transform the exact values, then give uncertainties, select and add noise Fields: obs.
origin_km1 × 3doublekmrequiredorigin of the new frame in the current frame [km]; [0 0 0] keeps the origin Validation: mustBeFinite.
axes3 × 3doublerequired3 x 3 rotation, columns: the new axes as unit vectors in the current frame, e.g. cf.axes of sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame; eye(3) keeps the axes Validation: mustBeFinite.

Outputs

NameDescription
obsa measurement set; to change the axes it must have all six inertia elements without uncertainties, as the exact values of sbtk.data.simulate have (or no inertia rows): a measurement is made in the frame it is reported in, so transform the exact values, then give uncertainties, select and add noise Fields: obs.

Description

origin_km becomes (origin_km - o)*axes and com_minus_cof_km becomes com_minus_cof_km*axes. The coefficients stay about the same point and are rotated degree by degree, with their covariance (exact, sbtk.internal.sh_rotation); every degree present must be complete. The inertia elements Ixx ... Iyz are recomputed as the elements in the new axes (axes'*I*axes); the libration row and libration_ratio use the new z-axis (C = Izz) and the principal axes in the new xy-plane; any other row keeps its meaning (its weights are transformed). A translation alone (axes = eye(3)) applies to any set. Use the same origin_km and axes for the body (sbtk.body.to_frame) and the interior or true model (sbtk.interior.to_frame).

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: truth, body, exact, unc.
spin    = sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame(truth, body, "spin");
exact_s = sbtk.data.to_frame(exact, spin.com_km, spin.axes);      % C21 = S21 = 0
obs_s   = sbtk.data.add_noise(sbtk.data.set_uncertainties(exact_s, unc), 1);

sbtk.data.use_uncertainties#

Give measurements the coefficient uncertainties of another data set (e.g. a precision file).

Syntax

MATLAB
obs = sbtk.data.use_uncertainties(obs, ref)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
obs1 × 1structrequiredmeasurements whose uncertainties are replaced (usually exact values from sbtk.data.simulate, before sbtk.data.add_noise) Fields: obs.
ref1 × 1structrequiredmeasurements holding the uncertainties to use, e.g. a precision file read with sbtk.exchange.read_shadr or sbtk.exchange.read_data Fields: ref.

Outputs

NameDescription
obsmeasurements whose uncertainties are replaced (usually exact values from sbtk.data.simulate, before sbtk.data.add_noise) Fields: obs.

Description

Every coefficient of obs that ref also has takes ref's variances and covariances; the others (e.g. degree 1 if ref has none) keep theirs and become uncorrelated with them (exact values from sbtk.data.simulate have none: give them with sbtk.data.set_uncertainties first). If the reference radii differ, ref's covariance is converted to obs.R_ref_km first: a coefficient of degree l scales by (R_ref / R_obs)^l. Moment-of-inertia uncertainties are not changed (sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma sets them).

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, interior.
shape = sbtk.shape.load("didymos_g_9309mm_spc_obj_0000n00000_v003.obj", "km");

sbtk.invert.choose_regularization#

Tikhonov regularization parameter by the discrepancy principle.

Syntax

MATLAB
lambda = sbtk.invert.choose_regularization(prob)
prob.opts.regularization = lambda;  fit = sbtk.invert.run(prob);

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
prob1 × 1structrequiredPrepared inversion; prob.opts.regularization is not used. Fields: prob.

Outputs

NameDescription
lambdaTikhonov parameter chosen by the discrepancy principle.

Description

The regularization term lambda * sum((drho_c / rho_mean)^2) damps the relative densities. Models with many components (a sector grid) or weak data need it to keep noise from producing large alternating densities. This returns the largest lambda for which chi^2 <= max(n, chi^2_min + sqrt(2n)), n measurements, chi^2_min the unregularized value: chi^2 may rise by about one standard deviation of its distribution. Bisection on log10(lambda) over [-2, 8] (9 solves, about 0.2 s with prob reused).

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, obs.
sectors = sbtk.interior.sector_grid([0 0.5 1], [-90 0 90], [-180 0 180]);
prob = sbtk.invert.setup(body, sectors, obs, sbtk.invert.options(background="bulk"));
prob.opts.regularization = sbtk.invert.choose_regularization(prob);
fit = sbtk.invert.run(prob);

Related functions

sbtk.invert.goodness_of_fit#

Reduced chi-square and chi-square test of a fit.

Syntax

MATLAB
[chi2_reduced, p_value, consistent] = sbtk.invert.goodness_of_fit(chi2, dof)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
chi2scalardoublerequiredsum of squared normalized residuals (with the full covariance) Validation: mustBeNonnegative.
dofscalardoublerequireddegrees of freedom: number of measurements minus the effective number of estimated parameters Validation: mustBeFinite.

Outputs

NameDescription
chi2_reducedchi2/dof; about 1 when the model and the stated uncertainties are right
p_valueprobability that a correct model gives a chi2 at least this large
consistentp_value >= 0.05: the model is consistent with the measurements at the 5% significance level

Description

With dof <= 0 (at least as many parameters as measurements) the test is undefined: chi2_reduced and p_value are NaN and consistent is false.

Example

sbtk.invert.run#

Estimate the densities for a prepared inversion (bounded, mass-constrained least squares).

Syntax

MATLAB
fit = sbtk.invert.run(prob)          % prob from sbtk.invert.setup

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
prob1 × 1structrequiredPrepared inversion from sbtk.invert.setup (or sbtk.invert.replace_data). Fields: prob.

Outputs

NameDescription
fitInversion result. Fields: fit.

Description

Unknowns: the background density, the relative density of each component, and the geometry asked for: the center of spheres, ellipsoids and tori with estimate_position (all coordinates, or those of a mask [x y z]) and the axis of ellipsoids and tori with estimate_axis = true. The total mass is an equality constraint and every component's density is bounded to [0, opts.rho_max_kgm3]. Measurements are whitened by the Cholesky factor of their covariance and the columns scaled to unit norm; the problem is solved with lsqlin (active set, or interior point if the active set does not converge). The geometry is refined by Gauss-Newton (at most opts.max_iter steps) with a trust region (opts.step_km for center coordinates, opts.step_deg for axis tilts): a step that does not lower the objective is undone and the trust region halved; it has converged when the objective changes by less than 1e-10 relative or a step changes every parameter by less than opts.geometry_tol of its step limit. Optional a priori constraints keep the geometry near its start (opts.position_sigma_km, opts.axis_sigma_deg), hard limits bound how far it may go (opts.max_shift_km, opts.max_tilt_deg), and spheres are kept inside the body. The parameters are listed by sbtk.internal.geometry_parameters. Optional Tikhonov regularization (opts.regularization) penalizes the relative densities. The covariance is the linearized one with the mass constraint eliminated (inequality bounds are not included; see fit.at_bound).

fit (a model: rho_bg_kgm3, components, random_field, origin_km, plus)

rho_bg_kgm3, rho_bg_sigma_kgm3background density and its 1-sigma [kg/m^3]
componentsthe components with the estimated relative densities drho_kgm3
drho_sigma_kgm31-sigma of each relative density
rho_kgm3, rho_sigma_kgm3density of each component (background + relative) and its 1-sigma
center_sigma_kmn x 3 1-sigma of the center coordinates (NaN unless estimated)
axis_sigma_degn x 3 1-sigma of the rotations about the component's first, second and third axes [deg]: the tilts of its axis and, for an ellipsoid, its turn about it (NaN unless estimated)
at_bounddensity at 0 or rho_max
resolved|relative density| > its 1-sigma
determinedfalse if the measurements (with any prior or regularization) do not determine all free parameters; cov is then a pseudo-inverse and the solution is not unique
chi2, n_obs, dofchi-square, number of measurements, degrees of freedom (n_obs minus the effective number of parameters, trace of the data resolution matrix)
chi2_reduced, p_value chi2/dof and P(chi2 >= observed) for a correct model
consistentp_value >= 0.05 (model consistent with the measurements)
labels, measured, predicted, sigma, normalized_residual
every measurement, its predicted value, (predicted - measured)/sigma
names, cov, corrparameters, their covariance and correlation
iterations, regularization, moi_labels, background, body, data_name
coef_about'origin' or 'center_of_mass' (from the measurements)
com_shift_kmmodel's center of mass minus origin_km: the point the predicted coefficients of degree >= 2 and inertia are about ([0 0 0] for 'origin')
frame_iterationsGauss-Newton steps on the model's center of mass (0 for 'origin')
frame_offset_kmchange of that center in the last step (below 1e-6 km when converged)

When obs.coef_about is 'center_of_mass' (packages read with sbtk.exchange.read_data, fields from sbtk.data.add_center_of_mass), the predicted coefficients of degree >= 2 and inertia are moved to the fitted model's own center of mass (exact translation), and the fit repeated until that center moves less than 1 mm. The model itself stays fixed: origin_km is the measured center of mass, from which layers and sectors are measured.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, components, obs.
prob = sbtk.invert.setup(body, components, obs, sbtk.invert.options());
fit  = sbtk.invert.run(prob);
sbtk.invert.summary(fit)

cmpComparison with the true model. Fields: cmp.

Description

Both densities are evaluated at points filling the body (24 radial shells per facet cone, 1.18 million for Didymos, each weighted by its volume); the true model's layers and sectors are measured from truth.origin_km, the fit's from fit.origin_km. About 0.5 s for Didymos.

cmp.R2coefficient of determination of the estimated density: R2 = 1 - sum w (rho_est - rho_true)^2 / sum w (rho_true - mean)^2, the fraction of the variance of the true density (about its volume-weighted mean) that the estimate explains. 1 = exact; 0 = no better than a homogeneous body; < 0 = worse than that.
cmp.R2_maxthe largest R2 attainable with the same components (weighted least-squares fit of the true density by the background and the components): the limit set by the choice of components
cmp.rms_kgm3volume-weighted RMS density error [kg/m^3]
cmp.std_true_kgm3volume-weighted standard deviation of the true density [kg/m^3]
cmp.componentscomponents with the same name in both: name, estimate_kgm3, sigma_kgm3, true_kgm3 (densities), deviation_sigma (|estimate - true| / sigma)
cmp.chi2_reduced, cmp.p_valuecopied from the fit

For many fits with the same components against one true model, call sbtk.compare.reference once and sbtk.compare.evaluate for each fit.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, truth, fit.
cmp = sbtk.compare.with_truth(body, truth, fit);
sbtk.compare.summary(cmp)
sbtk.plot.comparison(cmp);

sbtk.exchange.density_grid#

Density of a model at the centers of a cubic grid inside the body.

Syntax

MATLAB
grid = sbtk.exchange.density_grid(body, model, spacing_km)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.body.create Fields: body.
model1 × 1structrequireda true model (sbtk.data.simulate) or a fit (sbtk.invert.run)
spacing_kmscalardoublekmrequiredcell edge [km] Validation: mustBePositive.

Outputs

NameDescription
gridThe density grid. Fields: grid.

Description

Cell centers lie at integer multiples of spacing_km along each axis of the shape-model frame, so grids with the same spacing coincide whoever makes them; cells whose center is inside the shape model are kept (tested along rays from the center of figure, so every model of a body has the same cells). The density is the model's density at the cell center (random field included).

grid.spacing_km, grid.x_km (n x 3), grid.density_kgm3 (n x 1), grid.density_sigma_kgm3 (n x 1, zero here; sbtk.exchange.write_solution fills it from the fit's covariance), grid.member (n x ncomp: the cell center is inside component c)

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, truth.
grid = sbtk.exchange.density_grid(body, truth, 0.020);                % 20 m cells
scatter3(grid.x_km(:,1), grid.x_km(:,2), grid.x_km(:,3), 4, grid.density_kgm3, 'filled');

sbtk.exchange.read_data#

Measurements and body from a measurement package (sbtk.exchange.write_data format).

Syntax

MATLAB
[obs, body] = sbtk.exchange.read_data(folder)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
folder1 × 1stringrequiredthe package folder (README.txt, gravity_field.txt, gravity_covariance.txt, center_of_mass.txt, moments_of_inertia.txt, conventions.txt, shape model) Validation: mustBeFolder.

Outputs

NameDescription
obsthe measurements, ready for sbtk.invert: coefficients of degree 2..L with their full covariance, expanded about the measured center of mass (obs.origin_km), plus degree-1 coefficients 0 +- sigma that carry the uncertainty of the center of mass, and the moment-of-inertia rows Fields: obs.
bodyfrom the package's shape model (lengths in km), mass = GM / G and the package's reference radius Fields: body.

Description

A package of exact values (no 1-sigma columns, no gravity_covariance.txt) gives a set with NaN uncertainties: give it uncertainties (e.g. sbtk.data.use_uncertainties with the precision file of the test) before sbtk.invert.

The libration ratio (B - A)/C becomes the row (B - A) - ratio*Izz = 0 with sigma ratio_sigma * Izz, where Izz is the measured Izz if the package has one, otherwise the Izz of the homogeneous body.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: components.

sbtk.io.read_jpl_gravity#

Measurements from a JPL SSD gravity-field file (normalized coefficients + covariance).

Syntax

MATLAB
obs = sbtk.io.read_jpl_gravity(file, body, name, origin_km, degree)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
file1 × 1stringrequiredJPL SSD gravity file in MATLAB-assignment form (REF_RADIUS, NORMALIZED, NAMES = {...}, VALS = [...], COV = [...]), e.g. the OSIRIS-REx Bennu field Validation: mustBeFile.
body1 × 1structrequiredfrom sbtk.body.create; body.R_ref_km must equal the file's REF_RADIUS Fields: body.
name1 × 1stringrequiredname of the data set
origin_km1 × 3doublekmrequiredpoint the field is expanded about, in shape-model coordinates [km] (the center of mass of the gravity solution) Validation: mustBeFinite.
degreescalardoublerequiredhighest degree to keep (2 .. the file's DEGREE) Validation: mustBeInteger, mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual(degree, 2).

Outputs

NameDescription
obsThe measurement set: coefficients of degree 2 … degree with their covariance, coef_about = 'origin'. Fields: obs.

Description

The file is parsed as text (not executed). Zonal terms J_l are converted to C_l0 = -J_l (with the matching sign changes in the covariance); C_lm, S_lm are kept. The covariance of the kept coefficients is the full submatrix of the file's covariance (GM row and column removed). The mass is GM / G. Degree-1 terms are absent in such files (the expansion is about the center of mass); add them with sbtk.data.add_center_of_mass.

Example

MATLAB, from the help text
body = sbtk.body.create("Bennu", sbtk.shape.bundled("bennu"), 1190, 0.290);
file = fullfile(sbtk.root, "data", "gravity", "bennu_osirisrex_jpl_2019.txt");
obs  = sbtk.io.read_jpl_gravity(file, body, "bennu_jpl2019", [0 0 0], 4);
obs  = sbtk.data.add_center_of_mass(obs, [0 0 0], 0.001);

sbtk.plot.difference_from_homogeneous#

Gravity coefficients minus those of the homogeneous body, coefficient by coefficient.

Syntax

MATLAB
[fig, differences] = sbtk.plot.difference_from_homogeneous(body, sets, names, scale, frame)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredthe body: its shape model gives the homogeneous body (density M/V everywhere) Fields: body.
sets1 × anycellrequiredcell array of coefficient sets, each one of a measurement set exact values (sbtk.data.simulate), measurements (sbtk.data.add_noise), a package (sbtk.exchange.read_data), ... a true model truth from sbtk.data.simulate an inversion result fit from sbtk.invert.run: the field of the fitted model
namesrequiredone legend entry per set, e.g. ["true model" "estimate"] Validation: mustBeText.
scale1 × 1stringrequired"linear": the signed difference, with +-3 sigma bars for sets that have uncertainties (measurement sets with coef_cov); "log": the absolute difference, with 3 sigma drawn as a separate line Validation: mustBeMember(scale, ["linear", "log"]).
frame1 × 1stringrequiredthe axes both fields are expressed in (sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame): "shape": the axes of the shape-model frame; "spin": z along the axis of the largest moment of the set, x the shape-model x-axis projected onto the plane normal to it, as in body-fixed radio-science fields (the OSIRIS-REx field of Bennu). The set has C21 = S21 = 0, so the homogeneous body's C21, S21 show how far its axis of the largest moment is tilted from the set's; "principal": the principal axes of inertia of the set (x the axis of the smallest moment, z of the largest). The set has C21 = S21 = S22 = 0, so the homogeneous body's C21, S21, S22 show how its principal axes are tilted and turned. Validation: mustBeMember(frame, ["shape", "spin", "principal"]).

Outputs

NameDescription
figthe figure
differencesstruct array, one per set: name, labels (as plotted: C10, C11, S11, J2, ...), difference, sigma (1-sigma; NaN where the set has none), axes_deg ([tilt turn]: angle between the axes of the largest moment of the set and of the homogeneous body, and angle about that axis between their axes of the smallest moment, deg)

Description

Both fields are about their own center of mass, as radio-science fields are:

  degrees >= 2   the set about its center of mass minus the homogeneous body about its
                 center of mass (the center of figure)
  degree 1       the set's center of mass minus the center of figure, as C11, S11, C10 =
                 (x, y, z)/(sqrt(3) R_ref) in the axes of the plot: about its own center of
                 mass each field's degree 1 is zero, so this shows where the interior moves
                 the center of mass instead

sbtk.gravity.center_of_mass_frame moves each set to its center of mass and into the axes (it states how the center of mass of each kind of set is found); the homogeneous field is rotated into the same axes. Differences are fully normalized, in SBTK order; zonal coefficients are shown as J_l = -C_l0, so their difference has the opposite sign of the C_l0 difference. The reference radius is the set's (body.R_ref_km for truth and fit). One geometry is built per set (about 1 s for 49,152 facets at degree 4, about a minute for 3 million facets).

The plot shows how far the gravity field of an interior departs from that of a uniform density, and, against 3 sigma, which departures measurements resolve. The three frames show the same information: the spin and principal axes move the difference in orientation of the principal axes into the homogeneous body's degree-2 terms.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, interior, unc, components.
[exact, truth] = sbtk.data.simulate(body, interior, 4, "T1");
sbtk.plot.difference_from_homogeneous(body, {truth}, "true model", "linear", "principal");
obs = sbtk.data.add_noise(sbtk.data.set_uncertainties(exact, unc), 1);
fit = sbtk.invert.solve(body, components, obs);
sbtk.plot.difference_from_homogeneous(body, {obs, fit}, ["measured" "estimate"], "log", "shape");

Related functions

Mentioned in the help text

Implementation: toolbox/+sbtk/+plot/slices.m, line 1.

sbtk.plot.truth_vs_estimate#

Truth, estimate and their difference on two planes.

Syntax

MATLAB
fig = sbtk.plot.truth_vs_estimate(body, truth, fit)

Arguments

NameSizeClassUnitDefaultDescription
body1 × 1structrequiredThe body. Fields: body.
truth1 × 1structrequiredThe true model. Fields: truth.
fit1 × 1structrequiredThe inversion result. Fields: fit.

Outputs

NameDescription
figHandle of the new figure.

Description

Rows: truth, estimate (same density color scale), and estimate minus truth (blue = estimate too light, red = too dense). Left: plane z = 0; right: plane y = 0, both through the truth's center of mass.

Example

MATLAB fragment from the help text. Uses variables defined by earlier calls: body, truth, fit.
fig = sbtk.plot.truth_vs_estimate(body, truth, fit);

Related functions

Calls
sbtk.gravity.geometry
Called by
sbtk.io.report_comparison

Implementation: toolbox/+sbtk/+plot/truth_vs_estimate.m, line 1.

Reference

Data structures

SBTK passes MATLAB structures between its functions. Each structure has a fixed set of fields, listed below; the field names carry their units (see Units). Sizes refer to the Didymos examples (49,152 facets, degree 4) unless stated: n is the number of measurements, nc the number of components, nf the number of facets, L the highest degree.

A model is any structure with the fields rho_bg_kgm3, components, random_field and origin_km: a true model (truth) or an inversion result (fit). Functions that evaluate, plot or compare densities accept either.

interior: Interior model#

Created by sbtk.interior.create.

Input of sbtk.data.simulate and sbtk.gravity.forward. The background density is not part of it: it follows from the mass of the body.

random_field: Gaussian random density field#

Created by sbtk.interior.random_field, sbtk.interior.no_random_field.

A sum of 300 Fourier modes with random wave vectors and phases, δρ(𝐱)=a∑j=1300cos(𝐤j·𝐱+φj) with a=σ2/300 and 𝐤j drawn from a normal distribution with standard deviation 1/L per component, which gives the correlation exp(−|Δ𝐱|2/(2L2)). The field is defined at every point and does not depend on the expansion origin.

Fields of random_field (6)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
sigma_kgm3#scalarkg/m³Standard deviation σ of the density perturbation; 0 means no field.
corr_length_km#scalarkmCorrelation length L.
seed#scalarSeed of the random number stream; the same seed gives the same field.
k_per_km#300 × 31/kmWave vectors 𝐤j.
phase#300 × 1radPhases φj.
amp_kgm3#scalarkg/m³Amplitude a of each mode.

member#n × nc logicalCell center inside each component. Only from sbtk.exchange.density_grid.

gridcmp: Comparison of two density grids#

Created by sbtk.compare.grids.

Fields of gridcmp (8)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
R2#scalar1−∑(ρest−ρtrue)2/∑(ρtrue−ρ¯true)2 over the common cells.

out: Results folder#

Created by sbtk.io.new_run, sbtk.io.subfolder.

Fields of out (5)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
project#textProject name.

pk: Coefficient order#

Created by sbtk.internal.sh_packing.

Packed coefficient vectors are ordered C00, C10, C11, S11, C20, C21, S21, C22, S22, C30, …: for each degree, Cl0, then Clm,Slm for m=1…l. Sizes for L=4.

Fields of pk (6)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
deg#1 × 25Degree of each entry.
ord#1 × 25Order of each entry.
isS#1 × 25 logicalTrue for sine coefficients.
idx#1 × 25Linear index into an (L+1) × (L+1) matrix with C(l+1, m+1) = Clm.
n#scalarNumber of entries, (L+1)2.
labels#1 × 25 cellNames, 'C00' … 'S44'.

samples: Points filling the body#

Created by sbtk.internal.body_samples.

Each facet cone is divided into 24 radial shells of equal steps in the radial fraction; each shell is represented by its centroid and volume. Used by the comparisons and the random-field integrals. Sizes for Didymos.

Fields of samples (5)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
X#1179648 × 3kmShell centroids in the shape-model frame.
w#1179648 × 1km³Shell volumes.
ts#1179648 × 1kmDistance from the origin to the surface along each point's ray.
ds#24 × npskp−sk−1p for the shell bounds s and powers p=3…max(L+3,5).
nr#scalarNumber of shells per cone (24).

slices: Plotting planes#

Created by sbtk.internal.slice_planes.

A 1 × 2 structure array: plane 1 is z=0 and plane 2 is y=0, both through the geometry's origin.

Fields of slices (7)
FieldSizeUnitDescription
g#1 × 280kmGrid coordinates along both plane axes.

Reference

Error identifiers

SBTK raises an error instead of substituting a value when an input is invalid or a computation cannot proceed. Every error has an identifier sbtk:<package>:<condition>, usable with verifyError in tests. The messages below are the fixed parts of the message text; values inserted at run time appear as format specifiers (%s, %d, %g).

IdentifierRaised byMessage
sbtk:compare:differentComponentssbtk.compare.evaluateThe fit's components differ from the reference's or origin (e.g. a sphere position was estimated): use sbtk.compare.with_truth.
sbtk:compare:gridSpacingsbtk.compare.gridsThe grids have different spacings (%g and %g km).
sbtk:data:axisymmetricsbtk.internal.libration_weightsIyy - Ixx = Ixy = 0 (C22 = S22 = 0): the body has no preferred equatorial axis, so (B - A)/C is not defined.
sbtk:data:coefLabelsbtk.data.select_coefficientsThe data have no coefficient %s.
sbtk:data:coefSizesbtk.data.from_coefficientsC, S, C_sigma and S_sigma must all be (L+1) x (L+1) with L >= 1.
sbtk:data:covPositivesbtk.data.set_covarianceThe covariance must be positive definite.
sbtk:data:covSizesbtk.data.set_covarianceCovariance is %d x %d; the data have %d coefficients.
sbtk:data:covSymmetricsbtk.data.set_covarianceThe covariance must be symmetric.
sbtk:data:degreeOnesbtk.data.add_center_of_massThe data already have degree-1 coefficients.
sbtk:data:duplicateMoisbtk.data.add_moi_rowThe data already have a moment-of-inertia row named %s.
sbtk:data:incompleteDegreesbtk.data.to_frameRotating the coefficients needs every coefficient of each degree present; degree %d is incomplete.
sbtk:data:moiLabelsbtk.data.select_moiThe data have no moment-of-inertia measurement %s.
sbtk:data:moiLabelsbtk.data.set_moi_sigmaThe data have no moment-of-inertia measurement %s.
sbtk:data:moveOriginsbtk.data.move_originOnly measurements about the center of mass can move their origin; these are about obs.origin_km.
sbtk:data:negativeDensitysbtk.data.simulateThe interior has negative density (minimum %.0f kg/m^3): make the light components less light.
sbtk:data:noC22sbtk.data.add_librationThe libration ratio needs the measured C22 and S22 (they give the direction of the principal axes).
sbtk:data:noCommonCoefficientssbtk.data.use_uncertaintiesThe two data sets have no gravity coefficient in common.
sbtk:data:noIzzsbtk.data.set_moi_sigmaThe 1-sigma of the libration row is the ratio's 1-sigma times Izz / (M R_ref^2) of the Izz row, which these data do not have: set it before sbtk.data.select_moi.
sbtk:data:noIzzsbtk.data.set_uncertaintiesThe 1-sigma of the libration row is the ratio's 1-sigma times Izz / (M R_ref^2) of the Izz row, which these data do not have: set the uncertainties before sbtk.data.select_moi.
sbtk:data:noUncertaintiessbtk.data.add_noiseThe measurements have no uncertainties to draw noise from: give them with sbtk.data.set_uncertainties, sbtk.data.use_uncertainties, sbtk.data.set_covariance or sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma.
sbtk:data:noUncertaintiessbtk.exchange.write_dataSome of the measurements have uncertainties and some do not. Give all of them (sbtk.data.set_uncertainties, sbtk.data.use_uncertainties, sbtk.data.set_covariance, sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma) or none (exact values).
sbtk:data:noUncertaintiessbtk.invert.replace_dataThe measurements have no uncertainties, which the inversion needs as weights: give them with sbtk.data.set_uncertainties, sbtk.data.use_uncertainties, sbtk.data.set_covariance or sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma.
sbtk:data:noUncertaintiessbtk.invert.setupThe measurements have no uncertainties, which the inversion needs as weights: give them with sbtk.data.set_uncertainties, sbtk.data.use_uncertainties, sbtk.data.set_covariance or sbtk.data.set_moi_sigma.
sbtk:data:transformMeasuredsbtk.data.to_frameInertia rows can be expressed in new axes only from the full inertia tensor without uncertainties: transform the exact values of sbtk.data.simulate, then use sbtk.data.set_uncertainties, sbtk.data.select_moi and sbtk.data.add_noise.
sbtk:data:uncertaintiessbtk.data.set_uncertaintiesunc.coef_sigma_by_degree has %d values; degree %d needs one per degree.
sbtk:data:zeroSigmasbtk.data.from_coefficientsUncertainty of %s is zero; every used coefficient needs sigma > 0.
sbtk:exchange:correlatedCenterOfMasssbtk.internal.exchange_data_filesThe center of mass is correlated with the other coefficients; the exchange format gives them separately.
sbtk:exchange:covariancesbtk.exchange.read_datagravity_covariance.txt has no row for %s.
sbtk:exchange:dataSetNamesbtk.exchange.solution_nameData set %s is not named <team>-DATA<number>.

Validation

Validation and tests#

SBTK 1.0.0 has 152 unit and integration tests in MATLAB's unit-test framework. They run with

MATLAB
run(fullfile(sbtk.root, "tests", "run_tests.m"))      % about 6 minutes; writes tests/reports/test_report.txt

This page states what the tests check and with what tolerance, as written in the test files. It makes no claims beyond them. Unit tests use a small ellipsoid body (tests/unit/small_body.m); validation tests use an ellipsoid with semi-axes 0.5 × 0.4 × 0.3 km (20,480 facets) and the 9.3 m Didymos model with a bulk density of 2600 kg/m³ and Rref = 0.40 km.

Comparison with independent results#

From tests/integration/test_validation.m:

Test Check Tolerance
testKernelVolume The kernel's degree-0 integral of every facet cone equals the cone volume. relative 10⁻¹²
testEllipsoidClosedForm C¯20, C¯22 and the principal moments of a homogeneous triaxial ellipsoid against the closed forms C20=(2c2−a2−b2)/(10R2), C22=(a2−b2)/(20R2), I=M(b2+c2)/5, … relative 2 × 10⁻³ (20,480-facet mesh)
testConeScaling Kernel output for a cone scaled by s=0.37 against sl+3 times the unscaled integrals. relative 10⁻¹³
testSpherePointMassVsRays A sphere integrated as a point mass against the same sphere integrated along rays (as an ellipsoid). relative 10⁻³
testTorus Volume and Izz of a buried torus against 2π2Ra2 and V(R2+3a2/4). relative 10⁻⁴ (volume), 10⁻³ (Izz)
testShellSector A full-sphere sector between radial fractions 0.5 and 0.75 has volume (0.753−0.53)V. relative 10⁻¹²
testSectorsTileBody The 24 sectors of a sector grid fill the body exactly once. relative 10⁻¹²
testRandomFieldMonteCarlo Mass and degree-2 integrals of a random field (σ = 120 kg/m³, L = 100 m) on Didymos against Monte Carlo integration with 4 × 10⁶ points. 2% of the largest value
testExactRecovery Exact Didymos data of a core (off-center), torus and regolith: densities and the core center are recovered, starting with the core at the origin. 10⁻⁶ kg/m³, 10⁻⁷ km, χ2 < 10⁻¹⁰
testExactRecoverySectors Exact data of a 24-sector interior with random densities are fitted by the same sectors. χ2 < 10⁻⁶, densities within 20 kg/m³
testCalibration Over 40 noise realizations, the standard deviation of (estimate − truth)/σ. within 0.25 of 1
testFullCovariance The same with coefficients correlated by 0.6 and noise drawn from that covariance. within 0.25 of 1
testInertiaHelps Adding Ixx, Iyy, Izz to the gravity coefficients reduces every density uncertainty. strict
testDimorphosExact Exact data of degree ≤ 3 and the libration ratio only (no other inertia data): an ellipsoidal core and a regolith layer are recovered. 10⁻⁶ kg/m³
testTextRoundTrip Writing and reading the measurement text format preserves values, covariance, origin, seed and libration ratio, and the fits agree. relative 10⁻¹⁴; densities 10⁻⁶ kg/m³
testFromCoefficients Data built from coefficient matrices equal the original measurement set and give the same fit. exact; 10⁻⁶ kg/m³

Conventions and frames#

From tests/unit/test_exchange.m and tests/unit/test_data.m:

Test Check Tolerance
testDegreeTwoAndInertia The relations between C¯20, C¯21, S¯21, C¯22, S¯22 and the inertia elements (Moments of inertia). 10⁻¹²
testNormalizationCode The normalization function printed in conventions.txt gives N20,N21,N22,N30=5,5/3,5/12,7. relative 10⁻¹⁵
testShTranslation Integrals moved by the solid-harmonic translation equal integrals computed about the shifted origin, including inertia. 10⁻¹² of the largest value
testPredictionsAboutTheModelCenterOfMass For data about the center of mass, the predicted coefficients and inertia of a fit equal a forward model computed from scratch about the fitted center of mass. 10⁻⁶
testCenterOfMassFrameMatchesTheTrueFrame Inverting a measurement package (expansion about the model's center of mass) gives the densities of an inversion about the true center of mass. 0.2σ; χ2 within 10%
testFrameIterationWithSectors The center-of-mass iteration converges with layers and many sectors. offset < 10⁻⁶ km in fewer than 20 iterations
testNothingAboutTheInterior A measurement package does not contain component names, the data-set name of the model, the seed, the expansion origin or the true center of mass.
testExactPackage A package of exact values has the columns l,m,C,S, no covariance file and no uncertainty or noise lines; it is read back with NaN uncertainties, the inversion asks for uncertainties, and with them it fits. values 10⁻¹⁷; χ2 < 10⁻⁶
testReportStatesWhatApplies Uncertainties, noise, the sign convention of the products of inertia and the libration ratio are stated only when the package has them; exact values with the center of mass as origin in principal axes, or with x, y turned 20° about z, are described as such in conventions.txt, and the package's shape model has its center of mass at the origin. 10⁻¹² km; obj precision for the center of figure
testGridDefinition Density-grid cell centers lie on multiples of the spacing and the cells fill the body; grids of different spacing are rejected. volume within 5% at 50 m cells
testLibrationRatioUsesPrincipalMoments The simulated libration ratio equals (B−A)/C from the eigenvalues of the tensor, and the true tensor satisfies the libration row. relative 10⁻¹², 10⁻¹⁴
testLibrationAmplitudeFormula G=2e/(3k−1) against numerical integration of planar libration in a Keplerian orbit (e = 0.01; k = 0.07, 0.25, 0.5), and the inverse formula. 3%; relative 10⁻¹²

Inversion behavior#

From tests/unit/test_invert.m: exact recovery with ν=n−p; the mass constraint (relative 10⁻¹⁰); the homogeneous fit has the bulk density and ν=n; regularization reduces the norm of the relative densities and increases the degrees of freedom; the p-value of χ2=10 with ν=10 equals 0.44049; density bounds hold and are flagged; settings by name and value; starting values of the relative densities are not used; unknown inertia labels and inconsistent replacement data are rejected. testEstimateTorusAxisAndHeight: the axis of a torus (true tilt 4.5°) and its height (12 m), started 3.5° and 15 m away, are recovered from exact values to 0.02° and 0.2 m with its density (5 kg/m³). testGeometryLimits: a hard limit on the tilt holds, an a priori constraint keeps the axis at its start, and geometry asked of components without a center or an axis is rejected. testEstimateEllipsoidOrientation: the full orientation of an ellipsoid (the direction of its third axis and its turn about it), started 8° away, is recovered from exact values to 0.05°, and a limit of 3° on the turn holds. The sphere-position results of test_regression_baseline.m (including the number of iterations) did not change when the estimated geometry was generalized.

Reproduction of published and earlier results#

Test file Check Tolerance
tests/integration/test_bennu_paper.m The Bennu inversion of Cavale et al. (Icarus) (Bennu): core relative density; boulders; torus mass contrast; core center; background equal to the bulk density 1190 kg/m³; coefficients of degrees 3–4 not fitted by the paper. 1 kg/m³; 2%; 1%; 0.5 m; 10⁻⁹ kg/m³; 0.15 of the JPL 1σ
tests/integration/test_regression_baseline.m Geometry, integrals, sample points, simulation, noise, inversion, regularization choice, comparison and position estimation against values stored from the code before the toolkit (tests/reference/baseline_v0.mat). Results that include an ellipsoid or a torus differ because their ray crossings are now exact: the old code sampled 256 points per chord and missed rays that only graze them (the exact crossings equal 4096 samples to 10⁻¹⁵). relative 10⁻¹⁰ unless stated in the test; 2 × 10⁻⁶ with an ellipsoid or a torus

tests/unit/test_gravity.m Uniform body, mass kept by the background, center-of-mass shift, labels, non-star-shaped meshes rejected, components clipped to the body. testCenterOfMassFrame: about the center of mass degree 1 is 0; in principal axes C¯21=S¯21=S¯22=0, each degree's power and each degree's total variance are unchanged, and C¯20, C¯22 equal the values from the principal moments; a measurement set, the same set without degree 1, and a set lacking a coefficient.

tests/integration/test_maker_scripts.m The six HLP6 maker scripts in examples/ pass the code analyzer; make_didymos_3 and make_dimorphos_3 run, and their packages have exact values only, their own shape-model file with the center of mass at the origin, the frame stated in conventions.txt, C¯21=S¯21=0 (and S¯22=0 for Dimorphos) to 10⁻¹², every boulder or void of the model, and no local paths.

Longer studies in tests/studies/ (recovery over interiors and data sets, edge cases of the forward model against brute-force integration, uncertainty calibration) are run separately and are not part of the test suite.
